correctness.rationale: Within 1/2<lambda<1, 2<gamma<1+(1/lambda)2^(1-1/lambda), the finite-mobilization update yields s_next>=2 s^lambda>=2s for s in (0,1), implying finite first full turnout and the ceiling(log2(1/s0)) bound. On the full-turnout edge, the clipped individual-surplus choice yields signed alternation with absolute z_next=H^{-1}(min((gamma-1)z,1)), H(z)=((1+z)/2)^a-((1-z)/2)^a, a=1/lambda. H strictly concave, H(z)/z decreases from a2^(1-a) to 1, so exactly one unstable z* and only balanced/threshold/saturated amplitudes; each above z* reaches exact amplitude 1 in finite time. Uniform contraction of the relative committed imbalance while turnout is partial proves all small positive total turnout ends balanced; expansion L=(gamma-1)/H'(z*)>1 yields escape time log(1/(z-z*))/log L+O(1). Independent computation confirmed radical example z*≈0.479891135132 and different full vs half-turnout outcomes. Clipping convention is explicit and essential: original implicit cut otherwise may not be defined globally.
